publicPromptHygiene.policy: Captured public community prompts preserve third-party handles, plates, addresses, domains, promo codes and upload filenames verbatim by owner decision. Byte-exactness forbids redacting in place; this inventory does not change publication.
publicPromptHygiene.method: scripts/lib/public-prompt-hygiene.mjs scans raw text for named @handles and lowercase dotted social handles (excluding reference slots), domains/URLs, postal-code-plus-street addresses, numbered license plates, promotional codes and upload filenames. Pattern matches are candidates, not identity verification or a guarantee that all such text is detectable.

source-reference-gaps.policy: These rows are exact as published but incomplete by origin: source feeds delete reference mentions. Keep their captured bytes and informational compatibility flags unchanged. The owner may hide them.
source-reference-gaps.method: scripts/lib/source-reference-gaps.mjs detects orphaned reference connectors, empty assignments and missing subjects, and records capture input-asset counts where available. Counts corroborate gaps; upload totals alone do not imply missing text. This is a conservative text-pattern inventory, not a completeness guarantee.

records.name: DRAGON AWAKENING
records.sourceDescription: Transform your portrait into a dark fantasy warrior commanding an ancient dragon inside a cavern.
records.prompt:
Generate ONE continuous 15-second vertical 9:16 photorealistic live-action cinematic dark-fantasy sequence with deliberate internal cinematic editing.
IMPORTANT REFERENCE RULE:
<<<image_1>>> is the ONLY identity reference for the protagonist.
Use <<<image_1>>> exclusively to preserve the protagonist's recognizable identity: exact facial structure, face shape, eyes, nose, lips, jaw, skin tone, hairstyle, hairline, hair color and all distinctive natural facial features.
The protagonist in every shot must clearly remain the SAME PERSON as <<<image_1>>> from frontal, 3/4, side-profile and wider camera angles.
Preserve the person's natural gender presentation, age appearance and recognizable facial identity from <<<image_1>>>.
Do NOT preserve the original clothing, background, lighting, pose or photographic environment from <<<image_1>>>.
Transform the person naturally into the protagonist of this medieval dark-fantasy scene while keeping the face unmistakably recognizable.
CHARACTER DESIGN:
The protagonist wears premium realistic medieval dragon-rider clothing: fitted matte-black layered leather armor covering the torso, subtle overlapping leather panels, small dark metal rivets, reinforced shoulder and forearm protection, multiple worn black leather belts with aged metal buckles, black gloves, dark trousers and boots.
A huge heavy black fur cloak rests across the shoulders and falls down the back, creating a powerful silhouette.
A medieval longsword in a dark worn scabbard is secured vertically behind the shoulder/back. The sword remains naturally attached throughout the sequence.
The clothing is practical, worn and physically realistic — not cosplay, not glossy fantasy armor.
Leather absorbs most light but catches subtle edge highlights. Metal elements produce restrained realistic reflections. The fur is dense, irregular, heavy and reacts naturally to body movement.
DRAGON DESIGN:
The same enormous photorealistic dragon appears throughout the sequence.
The dragon has an ancient, intimidating, physically believable appearance: an enormous elongated heavy skull, broad muscular snout, powerful jaw, irregular rows of natural predatory teeth, dark charcoal-black and deep brown rough scales, thick layered reptilian skin, weathered scars and imperfections.
Multiple massive backward-curving black horns grow naturally from the skull and jawline. Smaller irregular horn structures and armored scale ridges continue along the head and neck.
Its eyes are deep amber-brown with a wet reflective surface, heavy eyelids and believable animal anatomy.
The dragon is NOT elegant, cute or stylized.
It feels ancient, dangerous and enormous.
Its head alone is several times larger than the protagonist's upper body.
Every dragon movement communicates several tons of physical mass: enormous inertia, slow acceleration, controlled deceleration, heavy breathing and subtle muscular resistance through the neck and jaw.
LOCATION:
The entire sequence takes place inside one enormous natural dragon cave.
The cave is monumental, ancient, damp and almost completely dark.
Uneven black and charcoal stone walls disappear into deep shadow. The ceiling is barely visible. The darkness extends far beyond the protagonist.
No torch. No handheld light. No magical glow. No artificial fantasy illumination.
Only faint motivated natural light enters through distant cracks and openings high above the cavern.
This weak cold-neutral light selectively touches the protagonist's face, black armor, fur and nearby stone while most of the cave remains black.
The same faint light gradually catches portions of the dragon as it emerges from shadow.
Subtle volumetric dust and cave haze become visible only where they intersect the light.
Deep negative fill. Rich blacks. Controlled highlights. Extremely restrained desaturated color palette.
The darkness itself is a major part of the composition.
0.0–2.0s — SHOT 1 — THE TURN.
Open directly on a cinematic medium 3/4 side shot of the protagonist inside the dark cave.
Frame approximately from the waist/chest upward.
Camera is positioned slightly to the side and subtly below the protagonist's eye line, producing a restrained low-angle perspective.
The protagonist's body initially faces partially away from the unseen presence.
Posture is upright and grounded.
Shoulders carry the heavy fur cloak naturally.
The protagonist slowly turns the upper torso, shoulders and head toward something enormous inside the cave.
The movement is controlled and realistic.
The dense fur follows the body rotation with subtle delayed inertia.
The body completes the turn and becomes almost completely still.
The protagonist's eyes initially remain lower.
Then the EYES slowly rise first.
The head follows only slightly.
The gaze travels upward toward a specific enormous living creature towering above and ahead, outside the frame.
Do not look into the camera.
Facial performance is restrained and realistic:
uncertainty → recognition → controlled fear → focused attention.
The lips remain closed.
The jaw subtly tightens.
The protagonist realizes something gigantic is watching from the darkness.
Camera remains almost stationary with an extremely subtle cinematic push-in.
CUT.
2.0–5.2s — SHOT 2 — DRAGON REVEAL.
Cut to a monumental wide shot inside the same cave.
The protagonist is now a small human figure near the lower portion of the vertical frame, viewed mostly from behind.
The protagonist stands firmly on uneven dark stone, facing deeper into the cavern.
Head tilted upward.
Body completely still.
Far above and directly ahead is almost total darkness.
The dragon is already physically there, but its enormous head is initially almost impossible to distinguish from the black cave.
Hold the darkness briefly.
Then the colossal dragon VERY SLOWLY advances its head into the faint natural cave light.
The dragon does NOT suddenly appear.
Reveal it progressively and cinematically.
First: only an ambiguous gigantic silhouette separates from the darkness.
Then: faint light catches the dimensional edge of its enormous snout.
Then: individual rough scales become visible.
Then: huge backward-curving horns gradually emerge from blackness.
Then: one wet amber eye becomes readable.
Finally: portions of its jaw and irregular teeth appear.
Large sections of the dragon remain hidden in darkness even after the reveal.
The enormous head slowly lowers toward the tiny protagonist.
The scale difference is extreme and immediately readable.
The protagonist appears vulnerable and physically tiny beneath the creature.
The dragon slightly retracts its lips.
Its enormous jaws slowly open.
It releases ONE deep, physically powerful growl.
The growl reverberates through the entire cavern.
The dragon's head moves minimally during the growl because of its enormous weight.
No rapid reptilian motion. No floating head. No exaggerated CGI movement.
Camera remains wide, stable and majestic.
The reveal should feel like an expensive live-action feature-film creature reveal.
CUT.
5.2–6.5s — SHOT 3 — THE COMMAND.
Cut sharply from the enormous wide composition to an intimate tight close-up of the protagonist.
Face and upper fur-covered shoulders dominate the frame.
The cave behind falls into almost complete blackness.
Camera remains subtly below eye level.
The protagonist's head is tilted upward because the dragon towers above.
The protagonist looks UPWARD and slightly off-camera directly toward the dragon.
Never look into the lens.
For a brief moment controlled fear remains visible.
Then the eyes harden.
The brow subtly tightens.
The jaw sets.
The protagonist refuses to retreat.
Without unnecessary body movement, the protagonist commands loudly and decisively:
"Dohaerās!"
ONE speaker. ONE short command.
Precise natural lip synchronization.
The voice is powerful, authoritative and controlled rather than hysterical.
The mouth movement is anatomically natural and accurately synchronized with the word.
The command produces a short realistic echo through the cavern.
CUT.
6.5–8.2s — SHOT 4 — ACCEPTANCE.
Cut behind the protagonist into a tight cinematic over-the-shoulder shot.
Only the back/side of the protagonist's head and the upper edge of the heavy black fur shoulders appear in the near foreground.
The dragon's gigantic face fills most of the space ahead.
The dragon is now much closer.
Its jaws initially remain partially open and its teeth are visible.
The protagonist remains absolutely grounded and does not step backwards.
After hearing the command, the dragon pauses.
The aggression slowly disappears.
The enormous jaws VERY SLOWLY close.
The dragon subtly rotates its head into a 3/4 angle.
One enormous eye becomes clearly visible and studies the protagonist.
Then the dragon voluntarily brings its huge snout closer.
Not an attack.
A cautious act of acceptance.
The head decelerates naturally as it approaches.
CUT.
8.2–10.2s — SHOT 5 — FIRST TOUCH.
Cut to a VERY TIGHT cinematic side detail.
The dragon has ALREADY moved extremely close.
Do NOT show the whole dragon head.
Because of its enormous scale, only a small wall-like portion of the side of its huge snout near the nose occupies one side of the frame.
The composition primarily shows:
a small portion of the enormous dragon snout, rough layered scales, the protagonist's black-gloved hand, and only a short section of wrist/forearm.
The protagonist does NOT fully extend an arm toward a distant creature.
The hand is already physically close.
The protagonist makes one very short, slow, careful movement.
Relaxed wrist.
Natural fingers.
The palm gently approaches the side of the enormous snout.
CONTACT.
The gloved palm softly rests against the dragon's rough scales.
Do not grab. Do not stroke. Do not repeatedly move the hand.
The hand simply remains against the creature.
Show physically convincing contact: realistic scale relief, accurate contact shadow, subtle glove compression and tiny movement of the scales caused by the dragon's deep breathing.
The dragon remains calm and still.
This moment is intimate, quiet and dangerous.
CUT.
10.2–11.7s — SHOT 6 — REALIZATION.
Cut to an extremely close 3/4-profile portrait of the protagonist.
Camera is beside the protagonist but slightly forward, allowing most of the recognizable face from <<<image_1>>> to remain visible.
Do NOT use a perfect 90-degree profile.
The protagonist's head remains tilted upward toward the dragon.
Chin subtly raised.
For a brief beat, the protagonist continues looking upward.
